Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Salt Lake City UT
500 PM MST Wed Nov 18 2026

.KEY MESSAGES, Issued 1120 AM MST Wed Nov 18 2026...


 
- A longer duration storm will come through the area in pieces
  from Thursday morning through Saturday morning with the highest
  snow totals across the northern mountains and valley snow
  possible Friday evening into Saturday morning.

- Freezing temperatures are increasing in probability for the 
  Virgin River corridor near Zion National Park Saturday and 
  Sunday mornings.
 
&&

.DISCUSSION, Issued 1120 AM MST Wed Nov 18 2026...
The 12Z KSLC sounding showed -11.5C at 700mb which
is on the low end of the forecast envelope which is what led to
the widespread valley snow yesterday. This has also led to our
first freezing temperatures of the season at KSLC which ties the
latest on record. Temperatures will remain 3-8 degrees below
normal through the next week. 

A transient ridge has moved overhead with mostly clear skies and
cold temperatures, especially for areas that have snow covering
the ground. This will be a short-lived dry period before a broad
slow moving trough pushes into the Great Basin tomorrow. This
trough will bring several rounds of precipitation through Saturday
morning. The first round moves in on Thursday with the heaviest
across southern Utah as an atmospheric river rounds the southern
periphery of the Sierras coinciding with the left exit region of a
110+ kt jet. Snow levels will start much lower with this system
with snow levels generally between 6000-6500 feet. Flow aloft will
stay southwesterly during the duration of this first wave which
will favor aspects that do well in southerly flow. 

This first wave of precipitation associated with the initial 
trough axis will exit by Friday afternoon. This will likely be the
only period of precipitation for the southern half of Utah as the
trailing wave Friday night into Saturday morning focuses on 
northern Utah/SW Wyoming. This limited duration across southern
Utah will keep snow totals generally between 4-8" for the southern
mountains.

A secondary trailing wave on Friday evening will usher in colder
air aloft with median 700 mb temperatures falling to -10C which
would be cold enough to bring snow levels down to valley floors
by Friday evening as winds aloft become west/northwesterly.
Guidance is split on exactly how this will play out. A more
westerly flow will favor areas of Weber/Davis county, particularly
the benches while a more northwesterly flow will favor Tooele and
Salt Lake valleys. Moisture will remain in the mid to lower
portions of the column through 00Z Saturday before becoming
confined to the lower portion of the column, but this could allow
snow to continue through Saturday morning for areas across
northern Utah that reside in the preferential flow regime. Snow
totals for the northern mountains will range from 10-20" with
higher totals across the preferred aspects of 24"+. Valley snow
totals will be between 1-4" once a transition from rain to snow
occurs.

50% of guidance have another system moving through the state on
Monday that could be cold enough for valley snow to accompany the
entire event, but the other 50% of guidance do not bring this
system through. Regardless, temperatures will be cold with the
first freeze of the season likely for portions of Zion and lower
Washington county Saturday and Sunday morning.



&&

.AVIATION...

KSLC...Another storm system will push into the area. Southerly winds 
are largely expected to continue, with some gusts around 20-25 kts 
developing late Thursday morning. VFR CIGS will gradually lower 
through Thursday morning. Shower activity will gradually increase 
late morning into the afternoon, but shadowing due to terrain may 
hold more persistent rain off until late afternoon. Gradually 
dropping snow levels will allow snow to potentially mix in Thursday 
night, or prevail especially in higher rate periods. When it does, 
MVFR to IFR CIGS/VIS will start to become more likely.

REST OF UTAH AND SOUTHWEST WYOMING...A broad area of low pressure 
will gradually shift into the region through the TAF period. VFR 
cloud cover initially above 10 kft or so will gradually lower by 
Thursday morning as moisture increases. Shower activity will then 
pick up by late morning or so, becoming more persistent through the 
afternoon and into the evening. Snow levels a bit above 6 kft will 
drop to around 5 kft late evening through the overnight, allowing 
higher elevation terminals or those where rates are strong to see 
snow mix in or become dominant. At those locations, MVFR to IFR 
CIGS/VIS will become more likely. At most area terminals, a 
southerly wind component will prevail, with some gusts during the 
daytime hours especially at more exposed terminals.
